label: adhesin
assay_summary: Deletion of hyd1A ablated the conidial rodlet layer and significantly reduced conidial hydrophobicity and adhesion to insect cuticle relative to wild type.
notes: Gene synonym hyd1 of Zhang 2011; UniProt entry cites both papers. CONFLICT: Zhang 2011 (PMID 21375591) reported no adhesion defect for the single dhyd1 mutant (only hydrophobicity/virulence), while Feng 2024 (PMID 39724799) reports reduced cuticle adhesion for dhyd1A. The Zhang 2011 double mutant dhyd1dhyd2 had additively reduced attachment.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: dhyd2 conidia showed decreased cell-surface hydrophobicity and decreased adhesion (quantitative cell-attachment assay); dhyd1dhyd2 double mutant was additively reduced.
notes: UniProt gene hyd1B, synonym hyd2; entry cites both papers. Renamed hyd1B in the 2024 nine-hydrophobin survey, which also reports reduced cuticle adhesion (smaller effect than hyd1A).

label: adhesin
assay_summary: Disruption of adh2 decreased conidial adherence to insect wing cuticle and attenuated virulence via normal cuticle infection.
notes: Metarhizium Mad2-type adhesin. Assignment of the paper's Adh2 to BBA_02379 is by UniProt protein/gene name (entry not cited by the paper). Note the paper's companion genes Adh1/Mad1 (J4US32) and Adh3 (J4WB32) were dispensable - no adhesion phenotype - so they are NOT entered here (see unresolved file).

label: adhesin
assay_summary: qid74 disruptants had reduced capacity to adhere to hydrophobic surfaces while multicopy overexpressors adhered slightly better than wild type.
notes: Cell wall protein; also protects against lytic enzymes, so the mutant is pleiotropic. Accession matched by organism/gene/strain (original qid74 cloning PMID 9600944, same strain CECT 2413); the 2007 phenotype paper is not cited by the UniProt entry.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: TasHyd1 deletion mutants were altered in wettability and severely impaired in attachment to and colonization of plant roots; phenotype restored by complementation.
notes: UniProt entry explicitly cites PMID 20507444; length 145 aa matches the ORF described in the paper.

protein_name: Class I hydrophobin DewA (spore wall hydrophobin)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: Deletion of dewA decreased conidiospore agglomeration, lowering both the fraction of biomass present as pellets and the mean pellet size at all pH values tested.
notes: Assay is quantitative spore-spore aggregation, not host adhesion. Caveat: engineered-surface work (PMID 22154865) shows plain DewA films do NOT support mammalian cell adhesion unless an RGD or LG3 motif is inserted, so DewA adhesion is surface/self-aggregation, not ligand binding.

protein_name: Class I hydrophobin RodA (rodlet protein A)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: Deletion of rodA decreased conidiospore agglomeration (reduced pelleted biomass fraction and pellet size); contact-angle measurements showed RodA contributes more than DewA to spore surface hydrophobicity.
notes: Same aggregation assay as dewA. UniProt entry is not cited by this paper; identity confirmed by organism + gene + hydrophobin annotation.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: Two independent MoFLP1 null mutants showed marked reduction of conidial adhesion (as well as conidiation and appressorium turgor).
notes: JUDGEMENT CALL - weak positive. The protein has a predicted signal peptide and GPI signal but the GFP fusion localized to the vacuole membrane, and the mutant is pleiotropic (conidiation, turgor), so the adhesion defect may be indirect. Sequence identical to B9VVP3 (gene MFP1, EMBL FJ608586, same lab, 349 aa).

label: adhesin
assay_summary: GP70-silenced strains showed a significant reduction in adhesion to immobilised laminin and fibrinogen, plus reduced cell wall rhamnose/mannose and attenuated virulence in Galleria mellonella.
notes: Moonlighting: the same protein carries 3-carboxy-cis,cis-muconate cyclase activity (matches the UniProt annotation). Silencing (RNAi), not a clean deletion; cell wall composition also changes, so part of the effect may be indirect.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: GP70-silenced S. brasiliensis strains had decreased ability to bind laminin and fibronectin, altered cell wall beta-1,3-glucan exposure and attenuated virulence in Galleria mellonella.
notes: Same caveats as the S. schenckii orthologue (silencing, pleiotropic wall changes).

label: adhesin
assay_summary: PAP1-silenced S. schenckii strains showed defective adhesion to HeLa cells, laminin, fibronectin, fibrinogen, type-I and type-II collagen, and elastin, with normal growth and morphology.
notes: No UniProt entry; NCBI RefSeq protein verified by eutils esummary (305 aa, S. schenckii 1099-18). Locus SPSK_00848 taken from the paper text.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: PAP1-silenced S. brasiliensis strains showed defective adhesion to HeLa cells and ECM proteins, impaired thrombospondin-1 binding and impaired biofilm formation.
notes: No UniProt entry; NCBI RefSeq protein verified by eutils esummary (360 aa, S. brasiliensis 5110). Locus SPBR_07403 taken from the paper text.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: Recombinant Pap2 bound strongly to immobilised fibrinogen, fibronectin and type-I and type-II collagen; anti-rPap2 antibodies blocked killing of Galleria mellonella by the fungus.
notes: No UniProt entry; NCBI RefSeq verified by eutils esummary (233 aa). Evidence is recombinant-protein binding plus antibody blocking, no deletion mutant.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: The recombinant, highly glycosylated SPSK_02764 protein bound type-I and type-II collagen specifically; preincubation of yeast cells with anti-SPSK_02764 antibody reduced killing of Galleria mellonella.
notes: No UniProt entry; NCBI RefSeq verified by eutils esummary (169 aa). Authors argue it is a moonlighting cell wall peptidorhamnomannan component.

organism: Paracoccidioides lutzii (strain Pb01; published as P. brasiliensis)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: Recombinant GAPDH bound fibronectin, laminin and type-I collagen in ligand far-Western assays; anti-GAPDH antibody on yeast cells and free rGAPDH on pneumocytes both inhibited adherence and internalisation of the fungus.
notes: Moonlighting glycolytic enzyme detected in cytoplasm and cell wall by immunoelectron microscopy. UniProt entry (EMBL AF396657/AY061958, same Goias lab) is not cited by the adhesion paper; the isolate used was reported as P. brasiliensis but Pb01 is now P. lutzii.

organism: Paracoccidioides lutzii (strain Pb01; published as P. brasiliensis)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: PbTPI localised to the cell wall and bound preferentially to laminin in peptide inhibition assays; purified TPI and anti-TPI polyclonal antibody both inhibited the interaction of P. brasiliensis with cultured epithelial cells.
notes: Moonlighting glycolytic enzyme. UniProt entry (EMBL AY037936, Goias lab TPI deposit) is not cited by the adhesion paper; same species caveat as GAPDH.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: The 30 kDa, pI 4.9 laminin-binding adhesin was identified as a 14-3-3 protein; the recombinant protein and an anti-14-3-3 antibody each decreased P. brasiliensis adhesion to A549 epithelial cells, and only laminin (not fibronectin or collagens) bound the 30 kDa species.
notes: Accession confirmed from the paper text: cDNA GenBank AY462124 (protein AAR24348) = UniProt Q6S9D7. Moonlighting cytoplasmic regulator enriched at the wall during host-cell contact.

label: adhesin
assay_summary: Immobilised recombinant PbEno bound plasminogen in a specific, concentration-dependent, lysine-dependent manner; soluble rPbEno competitively inhibited plasminogen binding to fixed yeast cells, and rPbEno increased association of the fungus with epithelial cells and phagocytes.
notes: Moonlighting glycolytic enzyme, surface-localised by immunofluorescence; previously reported as a fibronectin-binding protein. UniProt entry (EMBL EF558735, "The enolase of Paracoccidioides brasiliensis", 2007 deposit) is not cited by the 2010 paper.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: cutinase (cutin hydrolase, surface sensing for appressorium maturation)
assay_summary: The cut2 mutant has reduced extracellular cutin-degrading and Ser esterase activity and fails to form the penetration peg, but the authors explicitly show Cut2 plays no role in spore or appressorium adhesion or in appressorial turgor.
notes: Ideal hard negative: adhesion was measured and was unchanged. UniProt entry cites PMID 17704215.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: tetraspanin membrane protein required for penetration peg differentiation
assay_summary: The punchless (pls1) mutant differentiates appressoria with wild-type structure, turgor and glycogen content and attaches to leaf and cellophane surfaces, but cannot differentiate a penetration peg.
notes: Integral membrane protein of 225 aa (matches the paper); plasma membrane and vacuolar localisation. UniProt entry not cited by the paper; identity confirmed by organism, tetraspanin annotation and length.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: tetraspanin membrane protein required for appressorium-mediated penetration
assay_summary: The Bcpls1 null mutant differentiates appressoria normally on plant and artificial surfaces (polarised-growth arrest, apex swelling, wall reinforcement) but no penetration events occur; it still infects wounded tissue.
notes: Orthologue of M. oryzae PLS1. UniProt entry is cited by PMID 12372414 (same tetraspanin survey) rather than the knockout paper; identity confirmed by organism + gene PLS1 + 225 aa.

protein_name: Class I hydrophobin EAS (ccg-2, rodlet protein)
label: hard_negative
mechanism: conidial rodlet-layer hydrophobin (surface hydrophobicity and spore dispersal)
assay_summary: RIP inactivation of ccg-2 produced the easily-wettable phenotype with loss of conidial rodlet fascicles, and transformation of an eas mutant with ccg-2 DNA restored surface rodlets; the demonstrated role is spore hydrophobicity/dispersal, with no adhesion assay or adhesion phenotype.
notes: Included as a hydrophobin hard negative: the clade's best-characterised class I hydrophobin whose demonstrated function is rodlet-layer assembly and dispersal, not adhesion. UniProt entry cites PMID 1459460.

label: hard_negative
assay_summary: Purified native Sm1 triggers reactive oxygen species production in rice and cotton seedlings and induces local and systemic defence gene expression, protecting cotton against Colletotrichum; it has no toxic activity and no adhesion function was shown.
notes: Small secreted cysteine-rich surface-active protein of the same general class that is often mis-predicted as an adhesin. UniProt entry cites PMID 16903350. Related surface-active cerato-platanins do modulate surface wettability (PMID 33538393) but that paper shows substrate conditioning, not protein-mediated adhesion.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: Group-I SUN-family (beta-glucosidase/Sun4-like) secreted cell wall glycoprotein; maintains cell wall and extracellular matrix structure
assay_summary: Bcsun1 knockout strains show cell surface alterations that affect production of reproductive structures and reduce adhesion to the plant surface, reducing virulence; BcSUN1 is the single Group-I SUN protein in the genome and is weakly attached to the cell surface.
notes: FLAGGED. Adhesion phenotype on deletion but indirect/Ecm33-like mechanism; owner decision 2026-11-26 to label hard_negative. Gene ID Bcin06g06040 taken from the paper text (EnsemblFungi B05.10 protein database) and matched to UniProt BCIN_06g06040; 471 aa is consistent with the reported 48 kDa glycoprotein. The paper's second SUN gene (Group-II, Bcin07g06600) was not knocked out.

organism: Trichoderma harzianum (sequence from strain CBS 226.95; experiments in strain NJAU4742)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: Purified ThSWO bound crystalline cellulose and swelled rice cell wall cellulose, and formed O-glycosylation-dependent condensates; the dThswo knockout showed a significant reduction in attached hyphal biomass per unit root weight (qPCR colonization assay, Fig. 6D), restored to wild-type level by exogenous ThSWO protein and by complementation.
notes: Accession is the one the authors state they used ("The amino acid sequence of ThSWO was retrieved from the NCBI database (accession number: XP_024771705.1)"); verified by eutils esummary (499 aa, T. harzianum CBS 226.95) and consistent with the stated 52.13 kDa theoretical mass. Caveat: the attachment metric is a 15-day root colonization qPCR (attached hyphal biomass), not a short-term adhesion assay, and ThSWO's primary biochemical activity is cellulose loosening, so part of the effect may be substrate conditioning rather than direct adhesion.

organism: Trichoderma harzianum (sequence from strain CBS 226.95; experiments in strain NJAU4742)
label: adhesin
assay_summary: Isothermal titration calorimetry showed spontaneous, glycosylation-dependent binding of ThFFSL to fucosylated ThSWO (abolished against deglycosylated ThSWO); the dThffsl knockout showed a significant decrease in attached hyphal biomass on rice roots, and ThFFSL guided and accelerated hyphal growth toward coated surfaces.
notes: Accession is the one the authors state they used ("The amino acid sequence and predicted structural information of ThFFSL were obtained from the UniProt database (accession number: A0A2T3ZSN5)"); verified live (301 aa, fucose-specific lectin, T. harzianum CBS 226.95), consistent with the reported ~32 kDa. Lectin ligand here is a fungal glycoprotein (ThSWO) at the root surface, not a host receptor.

label: hard_negative
mechanism: class I hydrophobin conferring colony/cell-surface hydrophobicity
assay_summary: Single, triple and quadruple hydrophobin disruptants of B. maydis showed no change in colony hydrophobicity, growth, conidiation, stress tolerance, virulence or sexual reproduction, yet expressing hyp1 in an Aspergillus nidulans dewA null mutant restored the lost colony hydrophobicity, showing the protein retains hydrophobicity function.
notes: Accession mapped by exact length from the source the authors used: they took the four hydrophobins from the JGI Cochliobolus heterostrophus C5 v2.0 gene catalog and report Hyp1 = 117 aa (Hyp2 100, Hyp3 157, Hyp4 182); among the twelve C5 hydrophobin entries in UniProt those four lengths are each unique, giving Hyp1 = M2UQJ0, Hyp2 = M2UUF3, Hyp3 = M2URC1, Hyp4 = M2UIG9. CAVEAT: adhesion itself was not assayed in B. maydis, and the non-adhesion function (hydrophobicity) was demonstrated heterologously in A. nidulans, not in the native host.
